subject: Post-call recap & POC next steps — Veridian AI
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ariel Chung <ariel@veridian.ai>, Samira Patel <samira@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-31T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap & POC next steps — Veridian AI

Hi Ariel / Samira — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a proposed POC charter so we have alignment going into the new year. Please skim and flag any changes.

Top pain points you emphasized:
- Inference latency sensitivity for live chat: average target 150ms p95 for single-turn responses (current: ~800ms)
- High token cost for production pipelines — want better unit economics without dropping quality
- Observability gaps: token-level cost attribution and prompt/regression alerts

Primary goals for the POC (30 days):
1) Validate a 3x improvement in p95 latency for the main chat flow at 95% of requests
2) Reduce per-token cost by >=30% on representative workloads
3) Demonstrate drift/regression detection on a small prompt set and show alerting in the Console

Proposed POC scope (what Redwood will deliver):
- Environment: Hosted sandbox with customer data isolated; we will provision an evaluation model variant (quantized) for the pilot
- Workload: 10K monthly equivalent requests simulated across the same prompt families you shared
- Metrics & success gates: latency p95, avg tokens/call, end-to-end cost per 1k requests, false-positive/negative rate on regression alerts
- Prompt/eval plan: use the 120 prompt seed set you shared during discovery; we will add 30 adversarial prompts to test regressions
- Owners:
  - Redwood: Evelyn (engagement lead), Ben (platform/config), Marcus (observability/metrics)
  - Veridian: Ariel (product), Samira (infra)
- Timeline (target):
  - Week 0 (this week): access + SSO setup, share baseline metrics
  - Week 1: model/quantization config + initial runs
  - Week 2: prompt/eval iteration and alert tuning
  - Week 3: cost/latency optimization and final validation

Access/setup asks from Veridian (what we need to start):
- SSO test account with SAML metadata or one admin invite (see attached SSO doc)
- Sample of historical chat logs for the 3 representative intents (CSV, anonymized) — just 3k rows preferred
- Confirmation of any blocked IP ranges for the sandbox

Attachments included: veridian_data_schema.csv (sample schema you shared in the call), sso_connection_requirements.pdf (Redwood SSO checklist)

Open questions / decisions we need now:
- Do you want an on-prem style network isolation or is hosted sandbox acceptable for the pilot?
- Any compliance constraints (data residency, audit logs) we should bake in from day 1?

Next actions (proposed):
- Ariel / Samira: share SSO test creds + sample data by Jan 4
- Ben: create sandbox env and send provisioning link by Jan 2
- Marcus: draft initial dashboards and wire in the prompt set by Jan 8

I'll follow up early next week with a JIRA and a shared Drive folder for artifacts. Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if you want to walk the plan.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Engagement Lead, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com | M: +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Attachment: veridian_data_schema.csv (CSV stub)
Attachment: sso_connection_requirements.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & POC next steps — Veridian AI

Evelyn — thanks for the clear outline. Two quick notes from the infra/platform side:

- I'll stand up the sandbox (hosted) and provision an API key scoped to the Veridian sandbox. ETA Jan 2 COB. I'll post the env details to the Drive link you create.
- For the latency target: we'll start with the quantized 8-bit variant we discussed. If p95 doesn't meet target at the simulated QPS, we'll try a batch/serve tuning and fallback to a larger instance class. I'll log the tuning steps in the runbook.

Action items I picked up:
- Create sandbox + API key (Ben) — target Jan 2
- Small runbook: quantization knobs + kernel choice we used (Ben) — attach by Jan 4
- Observability wire (Marcus) — initial dashboard by Jan 8

I'll cc Marcus on the sandbox provisioning ticket so he can start mapping metrics names from the Console.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
